map.输入正则后，基于 token 展示简化状态转移文本图。: After entering a regex, shows a simplified state-transition text diagram based on tokens.
map.把正则表达式解析为可视化流程图。: Parse a regex into a visual flowchart.
map.：把正则解析为语法树（AST），再绘制为铁路图（railroad diagram: : Parse the regex into an AST, then draw it as a railroad diagram showing the matching path.
map.：直观呈现分支、循环与可选部分，便于理解复杂正则的匹配顺序。: : Intuitively shows branches, loops, and optional parts, making complex regex matching order easier to understand.
map.：高亮分组范围、量词作用域与断言位置。: : Highlights group ranges, quantifier scope, and assertion positions.
map.：调试与学习复杂表达式，降低理解和沟通成本。: : Debugging and learning complex expressions, lowering understanding and communication cost.
map.把正则渲染成 railroad 图理解结构。: Render a regex as a railroad diagram to understand its structure.
map.读懂别人留下的复杂正则：把铁路图铺开，看清分支、量词与分组的嵌套关系，再决定怎么: Understand a complex regex left by others: spread out the railroad diagram, see the nesting of branches, quantifiers, and groups, then decide how to change it.
map.`a(b|c)*` → 起始 a，循环分支 b/c 的状态图。: `a(b|c)*` → starts with a, loops over the b/c branch.
map.从左到右的轨道即匹配路径。: The left-to-right track is the matching path.
map.为什么图里出现了我没写的分支？: Why does the diagram show branches I didn't write?
map.多半是量词与可选符（?、*、{n,m}）造成的：它们在图上表现为「可跳过的回路」: Mostly caused by quantifiers and optionals (? * {n,m}): on the diagram they appear as "skippable loops" or "repeating loops," looking like extra branches but actually equivalent expressions. Also, non-capturing groups (?:...) and lookaheads (?=...) have special representations that are easily confused with normal groups.
